activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Equivalent Fractions with Pictures
activities.explanation: Equivalent fractions look different but represent the same amount. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same value to find them.
activities.example: 1/2 is equal to 2/4: both show one half of a whole pizza.
activities.question: Which fraction is equal to 3/6?

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Fractions with Guided Visual Support
activities.explanation: Use a fraction bar to compare equal parts before solving. Colour the pieces to check equivalence.
activities.example: Split the same bar into 2 and then 4 equal parts: 1/2 covers the same space as 2/4.
activities.question: Shade the same amount as 1/2 using fourths.

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Compare Equivalent Fractions
activities.explanation: Use equivalent fractions to compare quantities with different denominators. Find a common denominator first.
activities.example: 3/4 equals 6/8, so it is greater than 1/2 (which equals 4/8).
activities.question: Which is larger: 2/3 or 3/6?

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Add Fractions with Different Denominators
activities.explanation: To add fractions with different denominators, rename both fractions using a common denominator, then add the numerators.
activities.question: What is 1/4 + 1/3?

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Multiplication Patterns to 10
activities.explanation: Patterns can make multiplication facts easier to recall. Look at the table and notice how each row grows by the same amount.
activities.example: 6 × 4 means six groups of four — 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4.
activities.question: What is 7 × 6?

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Two-Digit Multiplication Strategy
activities.explanation: Break two-digit multiplication into place-value parts (tens and ones), compute each part, then add them together.
activities.question: What is 14 × 3?

activities.subject: Mathematics
activities.title: Multi-Step Multiplication Problems
activities.explanation: Real problems often combine multiplication with addition or subtraction. Read carefully and break each question into steps.
activities.example: Aarav buys 4 packs of 6 pencils and gives 8 away. (4 × 6) − 8 = 24 − 8 = 16 pencils left.
activities.question: A shop has 7 boxes of 12 mangoes. They sell 28. How many remain?

activities.subject: Science
activities.title: How Plant Cells Work
activities.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, which help make food from sunlight using photosynthesis.
activities.example: A chloroplast is like a small solar kitchen inside a plant cell.
activities.question: Which cell part helps a plant make food?

activities.subject: Science
activities.title: The Photosynthesis Equation
activities.explanation: Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight into glucose and oxygen. Understanding the inputs and outputs lets you predict what happens if conditions change.
activities.example: Without sunlight, a plant cannot make glucose and will not grow well even with plenty of water.
activities.question: What three things does a plant need for photosynthesis?

activities.subject: Computer Science
activities.title: Step-by-Step Algorithms
activities.explanation: An algorithm is a clear sequence of steps used to solve a problem. Steps must be ordered, clear, and finite.
activities.example: To make tea: boil water, add tea, steep, and serve.
activities.question: What makes an algorithm useful?
activities.answer: Its steps should be clear, ordered, and finishable.

activities.subject: Computer Science
activities.title: Search Algorithms: Linear vs Binary
activities.explanation: Linear search checks each item one by one. Binary search halves a sorted list each time, so it is much faster for large data.
activities.example: Looking for a word on page 1 of a 1000-page book is linear. Opening the middle and deciding which half to keep is binary.
activities.question: Why does binary search need a sorted list?
activities.answer: So that, after checking the middle, you can safely throw away one entire half.

activities.subject: English
activities.title: Build Simple Sentences
activities.explanation: Every complete sentence needs a who or what (subject) and an action (predicate).
activities.example: The cat sat. Subject: the cat. Predicate: sat.
activities.question: Add a predicate: "My friend ___".
activities.answer: Any action works, e.g. "My friend laughed".
